verses.text: The burden of the wilderness of the sea. As whirlwinds in the South sweep through, it comes from the wilderness, from an awesome land.
A grievous vision is declared to me. The treacherous man deals treacherously, and the destroyer destroys. Go up, Elam; attack! I have stopped all of Media’s sighing.
Therefore my thighs are filled with anguish. Pains have taken hold on me, like the pains of a woman in labor. I am in so much pain that I can’t hear. I so am dismayed that I can’t see.
My heart flutters. Horror has frightened me. The twilight that I desired has been turned into trembling for me.
They prepare the table. They set the watch. They eat. They drink. Rise up, you princes, oil the shield!
For the Lord said to me, “Go, set a watchman. Let him declare what he sees.
When he sees a troop, horsemen in pairs, a troop of donkeys, a troop of camels, he shall listen diligently with great attentiveness.”
He cried like a lion: “Lord, I stand continually on the watchtower in the daytime, and every night I stay at my post.
Behold, here comes a troop of men, horsemen in pairs.” He answered, “Fallen, fallen is Babylon; and all the engraved images of her gods are broken to the ground.
You are my threshing, and the grain of my floor!” That which I have heard from Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, I have declared to you.
The burden of Dumah. One calls to me out of Seir, “Watchman, what of the night? Watchman, what of the night?”
The watchman said, “The morning comes, and also the night. If you will inquire, inquire. Come back again.”
The burden on Arabia. In the forest in Arabia you will lodge, you caravans of Dedanites.
They brought water to him who was thirsty. The inhabitants of the land of Tema met the fugitives with their bread.
For they fled away from the swords, from the drawn sword, from the bent bow, and from the heat of battle.
For the Lord said to me, “Within a year, as a worker bound by contract would count it, all the glory of Kedar will fail,
and the residue of the number of the archers, the mighty men of the children of Kedar, will be few; for Yahweh, the God of Israel, has spoken it.”

footnotes.content: The prophet sees a terrible vision sweeping in like a desert storm—judgment coming on Babylon from the wilderness. Isaiah feels the weight of it in his own body, as if the news itself brings physical anguish. When God opens our eyes to the ruin of human pride, we can't stay unmoved.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Elam and Media were historical powers the Medes used to overthrow Babylon—Isaiah names the instruments before the blow falls. This is the Lord's word before the world's event; He speaks what He has already decided. The treacherous destroy the treacherous when the Lord allows it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Isaiah writhes in spiritual travail—his body speaks what his lips declare. He sees a great city fall, and it pierces him like labor pains. This is the anguish of watching God's judgment unfold, a reminder that the Lord's justice is never casual or distant from the prophet's heart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The rest he longed for—the twilight, the evening's peace—becomes trembling. When God pulls back the veil and shows us what is truly coming, our natural hopes shake. Yet in that shaking, we're called to trust, not the peace of evening, but the faithfulness of the One who sees.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Babylon's rulers feast as if all is well, unaware of the judgment at their gate. They oil their shields, but their feast will be interrupted. How often do we too ignore the Lord's warnings, clinking our cups while the foundations crack beneath us?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord sets Isaiah as a watchman—not with power, but with eyes open to see and a voice to speak. This is every believer's calling: to watch, to listen, to declare what God shows us, whether anyone listens or not.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The watchman must attend with great attentiveness—not glancing, but watching steadily. Horses, camels, donkeys—the signs will come. Faithfulness to our watch means staying alert when the world moves on, because what God has told us to see is always worth seeing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The watchman cries like a lion—with urgency and power—yet he also stands in loneliness, day and night, at his post. His faithfulness costs him rest, but he remains because the Lord stationed him. Every watchman knows this loneliness; it's the price of seeing what others miss.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The vision materializes: Babylon has fallen, and her idols are shattered to the ground. All the might and splendor that seemed eternal crumbles like clay. Isaiah's vigil has vindicated—what he saw in the spirit, he now announces as fact. The Lord's word stands when all else crumbles.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Isaiah speaks to Judah now with intimate authority: You are the grain I have threshed from my floor—you are His harvest, His people, refined and kept by His hand. What he has heard from Yahweh about the nations' fate, he declares so Judah will trust their God when the great powers fall.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A cry comes from Seir—the Edomites asking the watchman about the night: How long will darkness last? Is the siege ending? Dumah (silence) is Edom's judgment—not a loud overthrow but a fading into nothing. Many ask the watchman the same question: When will the night end? When will the Lord act?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The watchman's answer is tender and honest: The morning comes, and the night too. No escape, no simple relief—but truth: day follows night, and if you will seek, seek again. The faithful answer is not false comfort but reality grounded in the Lord's promise that light does return, though we cannot hurry it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Arabia's burden comes next—the caravans must shelter in forests, fleeing the sword. Arabia, so distant, still feels the shock of judgment rippling outward. No corner of the earth escapes God's reckoning when pride must fall.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: In that dark hour, the people of Tema show mercy—they bring water to the thirsty fugitive, bread to the fleeing. Even in judgment's shadow, human kindness blooms. The Lord sees this too, and His mercies are new every morning.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They fled from swords, drawn blades, bent bows—the full machinery of war. War empties the land and scatters families. In all this tumult and loss, the fleeing still find Tema's bread waiting. God's hand is never wholly withdrawn, even in judgment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Within a year—the Lord sets a time as precise as a contract's terms. Kedar's glory will fade. The Lord does not destroy thoughtlessly but purposefully and according to His word. His judgments are measured, and His time is always kept.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The archers of Kedar—mighty in their own sight—will be few. Their strength, their numbers, their arrows count for nothing when the Lord speaks. Not a word can fail; His mouth has decided, and the nations feel it. Our faith rests not on power we see but on the God we trust.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
